claim: Aedes aegypti transmit pathogenic arboviruses while the mosquito itself tolerates the infection.
source: Aedes aegypti transmit pathogenic arboviruses while the mosquito itself tolerates the infection.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that represents established knowledge about Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and their relationship with arboviruses.

claim: piRNAs derived from vDNAs are essential for virus control.
source: The piRNAs derived from these vDNAs are essential for virus control and Piwi4 has a central role in the pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including RT inhibitor experiments and knockdown studies.

claim: Piwi4 has a central role in the piRNA-based antiviral pathway.
source: The piRNAs derived from these vDNAs are essential for virus control and Piwi4 has a central role in the pathway.
evidence: This is supported by multiple experiments showing Piwi4's role in virus restriction and piRNA maturation.

claim: Piwi4 binds preferentially to virus-derived piRNAs but not to transposon-targeting piRNAs.
source: Piwi4 binds preferentially to virus-derived piRNAs but not to transposon-targeting piRNAs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunoprecipitation experiments followed by small RNA sequencing.

claim: vDNA molecules are acquired through a discriminatory process of reverse-transcription and recombination directed by endogenous retrotransposons.
source: Analysis of episomal vDNA from infected cells reveals that vDNA molecules are acquired through a discriminatory process of reverse-transcription and recombination directed by endogenous retrotransposons.
evidence: This is supported by circular DNA sequencing data showing virus-transposon hybrids and preferential conversion of viral RNA.

claim: vDNAs integrated in the host genome as endogenous viral elements (EVEs) produce antisense piRNAs that are preferentially loaded onto Piwi4.
source: Using a high-resolution Ae. aegypti genomic sequence, we found that vDNAs integrated in the host genome as endogenous viral elements (EVEs), produce antisense piRNAs that are preferentially loaded onto Piwi4.
evidence: This is demonstrated through genome sequencing, small RNA sequencing, and Piwi4 immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: EVE-derived piRNAs are specifically loaded onto Piwi4 to inhibit virus replication.
source: Importantly, EVE-derived piRNAs are specifically loaded onto Piwi4 to inhibit virus replication.
evidence: This is supported by experiments showing that viruses carrying EVE sequences are inhibited in a Piwi4-dependent manner.

claim: Ae. aegypti employs a sophisticated antiviral mechanism that promotes viral persistence and generates long-lasting adaptive immunity.
source: Thus, Ae. aegypti employs a sophisticated antiviral mechanism that promotes viral persistence and generates long-lasting adaptive immunity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing EVE-mediated immunity and the balance between virus control and persistence.

claim: RNA interference (RNAi) is a major component of the mosquito antiviral defense.
source: As in other arthropods, RNA interference (RNAi) is a major component of the mosquito antiviral defense (Blair and Olson, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Intracellular long dsRNA, such as viral replicative intermediates, are processed by Dicer2 into 21 nucleotide siRNA duplexes.
source: Intracellular long dsRNA, such as viral replicative intermediates generated during positive-sense viral RNA replication, are processed by the processive endoribonuclease Dicer2 (Dcr2) into 21 nucleotide (nt) small interfering RNA (siRNAs) duplexes, which are loaded onto the endoribonuclease Argonaute-2 (Ago2) at the core of the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC).
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of siRNA-mediated antiviral defense.

claim: Ago2 cleaves one strand of the virus-derived siRNA duplex and utilizes the remaining strand as a guide to target and cleave complementary viral RNAs.
source: Ago2 then cleaves one strand of the virus-derived siRNA duplex and utilizes the remaining strand as a guide to target and cleave complementary viral RNAs, thereby restricting viral replication (van Rij et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Arboviral infections of Aedes spp. mosquitoes and cultured cells lead to the accumulation of 24–30 nt long virus-derived small RNAs.
source: In addition to 21 nt viral siRNAs (v-siRNAs), arboviral infections of Aedes spp. mosquitoes and cultured cells also lead to the accumulation of 24–30 nt long virus-derived small RNAs (Scott et al., 2010; Hess et al., 2011; Morazzani et al., 2012; Vodovar et al., 2012; Goic et al., 2016; Miesen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Virus-derived piRNA production involves PIWI proteins.
source: Like germline piRNAs, virus-derived piRNA (v-piRNA) production involves PIWI proteins (Miesen et al., 2015; Varjak et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: v-piRNAs present characteristics supporting the idea that these viral small RNAs are produced via a ping-pong mechanism.
source: In arbovirus-infected cells, the v-piRNAs also present characteristics supporting the idea that these viral small RNAs are produced via a ping-pong mechanism (Vodovar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: v-piRNAs are not observed in virus-infected Drosophila.
source: However, v-piRNAs are not observed in virus-infected Drosophila, nor are PIWI proteins involved in the fly antiviral defense (Petit et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: PIWI proteins are not involved in the Drosophila antiviral defense.
source: However, v-piRNAs are not observed in virus-infected Drosophila, nor are PIWI proteins involved in the fly antiviral defense (Petit et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Aedes mosquito dedicates a smaller fraction of its piRNAs to target TEs compared to Drosophila despite greater TE invasion of its genome.
source: Despite a much greater invasion of its genome by TEs compared to the fruitfly, the Aedes mosquito dedicates a smaller fraction of its piRNAs to target TEs (Arensburger et al., 2011) and possess an expanded Piwi gene family compared to Drosophila (Lewis et al., 2016), suggesting a functional diversification of the Piwi family in mosquito.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Aedes mosquito possesses an expanded Piwi gene family compared to Drosophila.
source: Despite a much greater invasion of its genome by TEs compared to the fruitfly, the Aedes mosquito dedicates a smaller fraction of its piRNAs to target TEs (Arensburger et al., 2011) and possess an expanded Piwi gene family compared to Drosophila (Lewis et al., 2016), suggesting a functional diversification of the Piwi family in mosquito.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The expanded Piwi gene family in Aedes mosquito suggests functional diversification of the Piwi family.
source: Despite a much greater invasion of its genome by TEs compared to the fruitfly, the Aedes mosquito dedicates a smaller fraction of its piRNAs to target TEs (Arensburger et al., 2011) and possess an expanded Piwi gene family compared to Drosophila (Lewis et al., 2016), suggesting a functional diversification of the Piwi family in mosquito.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparative genomic data cited from previous work.

claim: Piwi5 and Ago3 have been suggested to be specifically required for the formation of virus-derived piRNAs.
source: For instance, Piwi5 and Ago3 have been suggested to be specifically required for the formation of virus-derived piRNAs, although knock-down of these proteins had no effect on viral replication (Miesen et al., 2015; Varjak et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Knock-down of Piwi5 and Ago3 had no effect on viral replication.
source: For instance, Piwi5 and Ago3 have been suggested to be specifically required for the formation of virus-derived piRNAs, although knock-down of these proteins had no effect on viral replication (Miesen et al., 2015; Varjak et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Piwi4 has been shown to be antiviral in dsRNA knock-down screens.
source: By contrast Piwi4, has been shown to be antiviral in dsRNA knock-down screens (Varjak et al., 2018; Varjak et al., 2017a) but a direct association of viral piRNAs with Piwi4 has not been shown yet (Miesen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A direct association of viral piRNAs with Piwi4 has not been shown prior to this study.
source: By contrast Piwi4, has been shown to be antiviral in dsRNA knock-down screens (Varjak et al., 2018; Varjak et al., 2017a) but a direct association of viral piRNAs with Piwi4 has not been shown yet (Miesen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work and sets up the novelty of the current study.

claim: Fragments of viral RNA genomes are converted into vDNA by reverse-transcriptases derived from endogenous retrotransposons during arboviral infection in insect cells.
source: Upon arboviral infection in insect cells, fragments of viral RNA genomes are converted into vDNA by the reverse-transcriptases derived from endogenous retrotransposons, leading to the accumulation of episomal vDNA molecules.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in the manuscript and previous studies.

claim: Episomal vDNA molecules serve in the amplification of the antiviral RNAi response in Drosophila.
source: These episomal vDNA molecules serve in the amplification of the antiviral RNAi response in Drosophila (Tassetto et al., 2017) and have been linked to vector competence in mosquito (Goic et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Episomal vDNA molecules have been linked to vector competence in mosquito.
source: These episomal vDNA molecules serve in the amplification of the antiviral RNAi response in Drosophila (Tassetto et al., 2017) and have been linked to vector competence in mosquito (Goic et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Integration of viral elements has been identified in all eukaryotes and for all virus families.
source: At the genomic level, integration of viral elements has been identified in all eukaryotes and for all virus families (Holmes, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Endogenous viral elements (EVEs) in insects are derived mostly from non-retroviral RNA viruses.
source: In insects, these endogenous viral elements (EVEs) are derived mostly from non-retroviral RNA viruses (Palatini et al., 2017; Whitfield et al., 2017), with Aedes spp genomes harboring approximately 10 times more EVEs than other mosquito species.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Aedes spp genomes harbor approximately 10 times more EVEs than other mosquito species.
source: In insects, these endogenous viral elements (EVEs) are derived mostly from non-retroviral RNA viruses (Palatini et al., 2017; Whitfield et al., 2017), with Aedes spp genomes harboring approximately 10 times more EVEs than other mosquito species.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: EVEs organize in large loci characterized by high LTR retrotransposon density and the production of high levels of piRNAs.
source: Parallel analyses of genome and small RNA sequences from Aedes mosquitoes and derived cell lines reveal that EVEs organize in large loci characterized by high LTR retrotransposon density and the production of high levels of piRNAs (Whitfield et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Piwi4 is upregulated in somatic tissues in adult female Ae. aegypti following blood meal.
source: Here, we demonstrate that Piwi4 is upregulated in somatic tissues in adult female Ae. aegypti following blood meal and restricts dengue virus replication in vivo.
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Piwi4 restricts dengue virus replication in vivo.
source: Here, we demonstrate that Piwi4 is upregulated in somatic tissues in adult female Ae. aegypti following blood meal and restricts dengue virus replication in vivo.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments in mosquitoes shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Piwi4 is required for the accumulation of mature v-piRNAs in infected cells.
source: In infected cells, Piwi4 is required for the accumulation of mature v-piRNAs and binds preferentially to antisense v-piRNAs (corresponding to the anti-genome viral RNA) and not to anti-transposon piRNAs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by beta-elimination experiments and small RNA sequencing shown in Figure 2.

claim: Piwi4 binds preferentially to antisense v-piRNAs corresponding to the anti-genome viral RNA.
source: In infected cells, Piwi4 is required for the accumulation of mature v-piRNAs and binds preferentially to antisense v-piRNAs (corresponding to the anti-genome viral RNA) and not to anti-transposon piRNAs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Viral RNAs are preferentially reverse-transcribed during infection.
source: High-throughput sequencing of episomal DNA accumulating during infection reveals that viral RNAs are preferentially reverse-transcribed, indicating that this antiviral system discriminates between self (host mRNAs) and non-self RNAs (viral RNA) during the vDNA acquisition process.
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The antiviral system discriminates between self (host mRNAs) and non-self RNAs (viral RNA) during the vDNA acquisition process.
source: High-throughput sequencing of episomal DNA accumulating during infection reveals that viral RNAs are preferentially reverse-transcribed, indicating that this antiviral system discriminates between self (host mRNAs) and non-self RNAs (viral RNA) during the vDNA acquisition process.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that viral RNA is much more abundant in episomal DNA than host mRNAs despite lower abundance in the cell.

claim: Piwi4 preferentially binds to v-piRNAs derived from genomic EVEs compared to v-piRNAs derived from replicating viral RNA.
source: Furthermore, Piwi4 preferentially binds to v-piRNAs derived from genomic EVEs and as compare to v-piRNAs derived from replicating viral RNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoprecipitation experiments comparing EVE-derived and virus-derived piRNAs shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Knock-down of Piwi4 results in a decrease in EVE-derived piRNAs and an increase of CFAV RNA accumulation.
source: Consistent with this observation, knock-down of Piwi4 results in a decrease in EVE-derived piRNAs and an increase of CFAV RNA accumulation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Aag2 cells infected with Sindbis virus engineered to carry EVE sequences lead to efficient inhibition of SINV replication in a sequence and strand-specific manner.
source: Furthermore, Aag2 cells infected with Sindbis virus engineered to carry EVE sequences lead to efficient inhibition of SINV replication in a sequence and strand-specific manner, and knock-down of Piwi4 upregulates virus replication.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Knock-down of Piwi4 upregulates replication of SINV carrying EVE sequences.
source: Furthermore, Aag2 cells infected with Sindbis virus engineered to carry EVE sequences lead to efficient inhibition of SINV replication in a sequence and strand-specific manner, and knock-down of Piwi4 upregulates virus replication.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Genomic EVEs, EVE-derived piRNAs and Piwi4 are central to the antiviral adaptive immunity in Ae. aegypti mosquitoes.
source: Together our results indicate that genomic EVEs, EVE-derived piRNAs and Piwi4 are central to the antiviral adaptive immunity in Ae. aegypti mosquitoes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The acquisition of vDNA provides a mechanism for long-lasting mosquito adaptive immunity.
source: Given that EVEs are stably incorporated into genome, these observations suggest that the acquisition of vDNA provide a mechanism to long-lasting mosquito adaptive immunity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the stability of genomic integration and the demonstrated antiviral function of EVEs.

claim: Piwi4 had the strongest antiviral effect in Aag2 cells in an RNAi screen against all seven Aedes Piwi transcripts.
source: We first confirmed the role of PIWI proteins in antiviral defense using a RNAi screen against all seven Aedes Piwi transcripts, followed by Sindbis virus infection (SINV; Alphavirus; Togaviridae). We found that Piwi4 had the strongest antiviral effect in Aag2 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the RNAi screen data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Piwi4 knock-down in Aag2 cells led to higher viral replication of dengue virus type 2 (DENV2).
source: Likewise, Piwi4 knock-down in Aag2 cells led to higher viral replication of dengue virus type 2 (DENV2; Flavivirus; Flaviviridae) and Chikungunya virus (CHIKV; Alphavirus) (Figure 1A, n = 4, Mann-Whitney U test, p<0.05).
evidence: This is demonstrated by growth curve data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Piwi4 knock-down in Aag2 cells led to higher viral replication of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV).
source: Likewise, Piwi4 knock-down in Aag2 cells led to higher viral replication of dengue virus type 2 (DENV2; Flavivirus; Flaviviridae) and Chikungunya virus (CHIKV; Alphavirus) (Figure 1A, n = 4, Mann-Whitney U test, p<0.05).
evidence: This is demonstrated by growth curve data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Piwi4 mRNA is transiently increased in midguts and carcasses after a blood meal in adult female Ae. aegypti mosquitoes.
source: To relate these findings to the actual insect vector, we examined Piwi4 expression in somatic tissues of adult female Ae. aegypti mosquitoes and observed transient increases in both midguts and carcasses, but not in the ovaries, after a blood meal (Figure 1b, n = 4, Mann-Whitney U test, p<0.05).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Piwi4 mRNA is not increased in ovaries after a blood meal in adult female Ae. aegypti mosquitoes.
source: To relate these findings to the actual insect vector, we examined Piwi4 expression in somatic tissues of adult female Ae. aegypti mosquitoes and observed transient increases in both midguts and carcasses, but not in the ovaries, after a blood meal (Figure 1b, n = 4, Mann-Whitney U test, p<0.05).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Depletion of Piwi4 resulted in a significant increase of DENV2 genomic RNA in both the midgut and carcass at 7 and 10 days post infection.
source: Depletion of Piwi4 (dsPiwi4, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, Mann-Whitney U test, n = 4, p≤0.01–0.05, double and single asterisks respectively) resulted in a significant increase of DENV2 genomic RNA in both the midgut and carcass at 7 and 10 days post infection (dpi) and a significant increase of infectious virus titers in whole mosquitoes at 10 dpi (Figure 1c, n = 4, Mann-Whitney U test, p≤0.05).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Depletion of Piwi4 resulted in a significant increase of infectious DENV2 virus titers in whole mosquitoes at 10 dpi.
source: Depletion of Piwi4 (dsPiwi4, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, Mann-Whitney U test, n = 4, p≤0.01–0.05, double and single asterisks respectively) resulted in a significant increase of DENV2 genomic RNA in both the midgut and carcass at 7 and 10 days post infection (dpi) and a significant increase of infectious virus titers in whole mosquitoes at 10 dpi (Figure 1c, n = 4, Mann-Whitney U test, p≤0.05).
evidence: This is demonstrated by plaque assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Piwi4 mediates antiviral defense in Ae. aegypti somatic tissues.
source: These results indicate that Piwi4 mediates antiviral defense not only in cultured Aag2 cells but also in Ae. aegypti somatic tissues.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vivo experiments in mosquitoes.

claim: In control dsRNA-treated cells, both SINV-derived siRNAs (v-siRNAs, 21 nt long) and SINV-derived piRNAs (v-piRNAs, 24–30 nt long) accumulated during infection.
source: In control dsRNA-treated cells, both SINV-derived siRNAs (v-siRNAs, 21 nt long) and SINV-derived piRNAs (v-piRNAs, 24–30 nt long) accumulated during infection (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by small RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The 21 nt v-siRNAs are uniformly derived from the entire viral genome and correspond to both the sense and antisense strands of the genome.
source: The 21 nt v-siRNAs, are uniformly derived from the entire viral genome and correspond to both the sense and antisense strands of the genome (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by mapping data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 24 to 30 nt v-piRNAs were asymmetrically distributed with respect to strand polarity and position on the virus genome.
source: In contrast, 24 to 30 nt v-piRNAs were asymmetrically distributed with respect to strand polarity and position on the virus genome (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by mapping data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The overall size distribution of v-piRNAs was not affected by Piwi4 knock down.
source: As previously described (Miesen et al., 2015; Varjak et al., 2017a), the overall size distribution of v-piRNAs was not affected by Piwi4 knock down.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and data in the manuscript.

claim: Analysis of virus-derived small RNAs after ß-elimination showed a decrease in mature v-piRNAs in Piwi4 knock-down samples.
source: Analysis of virus-derived small RNAs after ß-elimination showed a decrease in mature v-piRNAs in Piwi4 knock-down samples (Figure 2B), suggesting a role for Piwi4 in v-piRNA maturation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by beta-elimination experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Piwi4 has a role in v-piRNA maturation.
source: Analysis of virus-derived small RNAs after ß-elimination showed a decrease in mature v-piRNAs in Piwi4 knock-down samples (Figure 2B), suggesting a role for Piwi4 in v-piRNA maturation.
evidence: This is inferred from the beta-elimination experiments.

claim: The large accumulation of sense v-piRNAs from the 5'-end of SINV subgenomic RNA is consistent with a model in which piRNA ping-pong amplification correlates with the abundance of RNA target.
source: The large accumulation of sense v-piRNAs from the 5'-end of SINV subgenomic RNA (genome 7611–11703 nt) is consistent with a model in which piRNA ping-pong amplification correlates with the abundance of RNA target (for instance, SINV subgenomic RNA) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed distribution of v-piRNAs.

claim: Knockdown of either Piwi4 or Ago3 reduced the abundance of mature v-piRNAs.
source: Knockdown of either Piwi4 or Ago3 reduced the abundance of mature v-piRNAs (resistant to ß-elimination, Figure 2D) and transposon-derived piRNAs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by beta-elimination experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Knockdown of either Piwi4 or Ago3 reduced the abundance of mature transposon-derived piRNAs.
source: Knockdown of either Piwi4 or Ago3 reduced the abundance of mature v-piRNAs (resistant to ß-elimination, Figure 2D) and transposon-derived piRNAs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by beta-elimination experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Knockdown of Piwi4 or Ago2, but not Ago3, resulted in complete depletion of mature v-siRNAs.
source: However, knockdown of Piwi4 or Ago2, but not Ago3, resulted in complete depletion of mature v-siRNAs (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by beta-elimination experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Piwi4 is involved in v-piRNA and v-siRNA maturation but appears to make a minor contribution to their initial production.
source: Our results indicate that Piwi4 is involved in v-piRNA and v-siRNA maturation but appears to make a minor contribution to their initial production (see Discussion).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on knockdown effects.

claim: Piwi4-associated small RNAs were significantly enriched for antisense SINV-derived piRNAs.
source: Contrary to previous reports that did not normalize to input small RNA content, we found that Piwi4 bound to v-piRNAs and that Piwi4-associated small RNAs were significantly enriched for antisense SINV-derived piRNAs (Figure 3A, antisense vs sense v-piRNAs, 2, p<2.2e-16).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoprecipitation followed by small RNA sequencing shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The enrichment of antisense v-piRNAs in Piwi4 pull-down (27–29 nt) was three fold higher than for other sizes of virus-derived small RNAs, including v-siRNAs (21-22nt).
source: The enrichment of antisense v-piRNAs in Piwi4 pull-down (27–29 nt) was three fold higher than for other sizes of virus-derived small RNAs, including v-siRNAs (21-22nt).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Antisense v-piRNAs were significantly enriched in Piwi4-bound fractions at a 95% confidence level.
source: Based on the bootstrap distribution, we calculated the 95% confidence intervals for the enrichment of each size of antisense small RNAs (error bars in Figure 3A) and found that they did not overlap between 27 and 28 nt antisense v-piRNAs and the all other antisense viRNAs. We thus conclude that antisense v-piRNAs were significantly enriched in Piwi4-bound fractions (at a 95% confidence level).
evidence: This is demonstrated by statistical analysis of immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Piwi4-associated v-piRNAs displayed a strong sequence bias with uracil as the most frequent base at the most-5' position.
source: In addition, Piwi4-associated v-piRNAs displayed a strong sequence bias, in which uracil is the most frequent base observed at the most-5' position (Figure 3B), a signature of Piwi-bound piRNAs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Piwi4 did not significantly associate with TE-derived piRNAs.
source: In contrast, Piwi4 did not significantly associate with TE-derived piRNAs (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Piwi4 interacts with Ago2.
source: In agreement with a recent study (Varjak et al., 2017a), we found that Piwi4 interacts with Ago2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and supported by a citation.

claim: The siRNA and piRNA pathways are linked through Piwi4, which may act as a hub to coordinate production of antiviral small RNAs.
source: Because knock-down of Piwi4 expression affects v-siRNAs production (Figure 2D) but does not specifically bind to them (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), our results suggest that the siRNA and piRNA pathways are linked through Piwi4, which may act as a hub to coordinate production of antiviral small RNAs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed effects of Piwi4 knockdown and binding specificity.

claim: Reverse transcriptase inhibitors AZT and Stavudine/d4T prevent production of vDNA in SINV-infected Aag2 cells.
source: We also observed that reverse transcriptase (RT) inhibitors AZT and Stavudine/d4T prevent production of vDNA in SINV-infected Aag2 cells (Figure 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCR data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Treatment with RT inhibitors resulted in an increase in SINV replication.
source: Furthermore, treatment with RT inhibitors resulted in an increase SINV replication (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: AZT and d4T treatments resulted in a significant reduction of v-piRNA reads.
source: Importantly, AZT and d4T treatments resulted in a significant reduction of v-piRNA reads but caused increased production of v-siRNAs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by small RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: AZT and d4T treatments caused increased production of v-siRNAs.
source: Importantly, AZT and d4T treatments resulted in a significant reduction of v-piRNA reads but caused increased production of v-siRNAs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by small RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Reverse transcription of viral genomes and production of piRNAs are essential components of the mosquito antiviral response.
source: These results provide a direct evidence that reverse transcription of viral genomes and production of piRNAs are essential components of the mosquito antiviral response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RT inhibitor experiments.

claim: Piwi4 and vDNA synthesis are essential for control of virus replication in mosquito cells.
source: Indeed, even if siRNAs are normally produced in Piwi4-depleted cells, we observed a significant increase in SINV genomic RNA accumulation, thus Piwi4 and vDNA synthesis are essential for control of virus replication in mosquito cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined results of Piwi4 knockdown and RT inhibitor experiments.

claim: Virus infection of mosquito cells induces the synthesis of vDNA, which serves as a template for v-piRNA precursor production.
source: Our data, together with previous observations (Goic et al., 2013; Goic et al., 2016), suggest a model in which virus infection of mosquito cells induces the synthesis of vDNA, which in turn serves as a template for v-piRNA precursor production, which are then processed into mature antiviral v-piRNA by Piwi4 to repress viral replication (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data and previous studies.

claim: PCR amplification of circular episomal DNA prepared from SINV-infected Aag2 cells with SINV genome-specific primers yielded a greater amplicon concentration than SINV-specific amplification of genomic DNA prep.
source: In support of this model, we observed that PCR amplification of circular episomal DNA prepared from SINV-infected Aag2 cells with SINV genome-specific primers yielded a greater amplicon concentration than SINV-specific amplification of genomic DNA prep (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Circular DNA preparations from SINV-infected Aag2 cells contained a significant enrichment of reads mapping to transposons (10–22% of total reads).
source: In addition to sequences derived from the circular mitochondrial genome (1% of total reads), we found that our preparations contained a significant enrichment of reads mapping to transposons (10–22% of total reads).
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data.

claim: Transposon sequences in circular DNA came almost exclusively from retrotransposons.
source: Transposon sequences came almost exclusively from retrotransposons, as expected due to a cytoplasmic step in their replication cycle.
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data and is consistent with the biology of retrotransposons.

claim: LTR-retrotransposons (Ty1, Ty3 and Pao Bel) were the most abundant sub-class observed in circular DNA preparations.
source: LTR-retrotransposons (Ty1, Ty3 and Pao Bel) were the most abundant sub-class observed (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: More than 1200 reads in the circular DNA enriched fraction mapped throughout most of the SINV genome.
source: Importantly, we also observed more than 1200 reads in the circular DNA enriched fraction mapping throughout most of the SINV genome (Figure 5D,i) with two regions less covered by vDNA (between 3500–4000 nt and 7500–8000 nt), corresponding to the NSP2 ORF and the start of the subgenomic RNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Two regions of the SINV genome were less covered by vDNA (between 3500–4000 nt and 7500–8000 nt), corresponding to the NSP2 ORF and the start of the subgenomic RNA.
source: Importantly, we also observed more than 1200 reads in the circular DNA enriched fraction mapping throughout most of the SINV genome (Figure 5D,i) with two regions less covered by vDNA (between 3500–4000 nt and 7500–8000 nt), corresponding to the NSP2 ORF and the start of the subgenomic RNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: More than 200 hybrids between SINV and the most abundant LTR-retrotransposon sequences were found in circular DNA.
source: We found more than 200 hybrids between SINV and the most abundant LTR-retrotransposon sequences (Figures 5E and 70 with Ty3 and 132 with Ty1 elements).
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Recombination between SINV and Ty3/gypsy Element73 occurred in the virus 5'UTR, the non-structural viral genes and in the subgenomic viral RNA that contains the structural genes.
source: Furthermore, mapping of hybrid reads from the most prevalent recombinants (SINV-Ty3/gypsy Element73) showed that recombination occurred in the virus 5'UTR, the non-structural viral genes and in the subgenomic viral RNA that contains the structural genes (Figure 5F,i and ii).
evidence: This is demonstrated by mapping data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The broad coverage of the SINV genome by SINV-only derived vDNA fragments suggests little bias in the recombination between LTR-retrotransposons and SINV mRNA.
source: In combination with the broad coverage of the SINV genome by the other SINV-only derived vDNA fragments (Figure 5D,i), our data suggest little bias in the recombination between LTR-retrotransposons and SINV mRNA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed distribution of vDNA reads.

claim: CFAV-only and CFAV-LTR transposon hybrid reads appeared to originate and cover almost the entire viral genome.
source: Similarly, CFAV-only and CFAV-LTR transposon hybrids reads (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C) appeared to originate and cover almost the entire viral genome.
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Recombination between viral RNA and transposons is not driven by sequence homology.
source: This further suggests that recombination is not driven by sequence homology.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of bias in recombination sites.

claim: CFAV recombinants were found mostly associated with Ty1 elements.
source: Unlike SINV, CFAV recombinants were found mostly associated with Ty1 elements (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Direct evidence of viral genome fragment conversion into circular vDNA was found in DENV infected Aag2 cells.
source: We also found direct evidence of viral genome fragment conversion into circular vDNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1Di and ii) in DENV infected Aag2 cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Only a small fraction of known expressed Aag2 mRNAs were found to have derived sequences in the episomal DNAs reads (~7.5% of known expressed mRNAs; 1093 out of 14612).
source: Only a small fraction of known expressed Aag2 mRNAs were found to have derived sequences in the episomal DNAs reads (~7.5% of known expressed mRNAs; 1093 out of 14612).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of circular DNA sequencing data compared to transcriptome data.

claim: There was no correlation between mRNA and episomal DNA abundance (R = 0.0045).
source: Furthermore, there was no correlation between mRNA and episomal DNA abundance (R = 0.0045, Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: No reads were detected from the top 54 most abundant mRNAs in episomal DNA.
source: We detected no reads derived from the top 54 most abundant mRNAs, which account for 32% of all transcripts, and found no correlation between mRNA length and their enrichment in episomal DNA (R = 0.0786, Figure 5H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of circular DNA sequencing data.

claim: There was no correlation between mRNA length and their enrichment in episomal DNA (R = 0.0786).
source: We detected no reads derived from the top 54 most abundant mRNAs, which account for 32% of all transcripts, and found no correlation between mRNA length and their enrichment in episomal DNA (R = 0.0786, Figure 5H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The number of SINV vDNA reads was higher than for the most abundant host mRNA-derived episomal DNA.
source: Indeed, the number of SINV vDNA reads was higher than for the most abundant host mRNA-derived episomal DNA (586 and 256 reads, for SINV and Aag2 transcript AAEL006357, respectively).
evidence: This is demonstrated by circular DNA sequencing data.

claim: Reverse transcription and recombination with retrotransposons is a highly specific mechanism, which preferentially converts viral RNA into vDNA.
source: Our results indicate that reverse transcription and recombination with retrotransposons is a highly specific mechanism, which preferentially converts viral RNA into vDNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of episomal DNA composition.

claim: vDNA is acquired by the specific incorporation of viral RNA into retrotransposon replication complexes, followed by reverse transcription and recombination between the transposon and virus genome.
source: Together, these data suggest a model in which vDNA is acquired by the specific incorporation of viral RNA into retrotransposon replication complexes, followed by reverse transcription and recombination between the transposon and virus genome.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data.

claim: A CFAV-derived EVE was found within contig 000933F in the Aag2 genome.
source: Among the EVEs identified in our new Aag2 genome (Whitfield et al., 2017, we found a CFAV-derived EVE within contig 000933F.
evidence: This is demonstrated by genome sequencing and analysis.

claim: The CFAV-derived EVE corresponds to the CFAV NS2A gene coding region and is flanked by long-terminal repeats (LTR) and gag Ty3-gypsy retrotransposon sequences.
source: This fragment corresponds to the CFAV NS2A gene coding region and it is flanked by long-terminal repeats (LTR) and gag Ty3-gypsy retrotransposon sequences (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by genome sequencing and annotation shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The CFAV/Ty3 gypsy sequence is inserted into a piRNA producing cluster among other LTR retrotransposons and EVEs.
source: This CFAV/Ty3 gypsy sequence is inserted into a piRNA producing cluster (piRNA cluster) among other LTR retrotransposons and EVEs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by genome sequencing and small RNA mapping.

claim: The piRNA cluster containing the CFAV EVE is transcriptionally active, producing antisense piRNAs targeting CFAV and members of other viral families.
source: This piRNA cluster is transcriptionally active, producing antisense piRNAs targeting CFAV and members of other viral families, such as Rhabdoviridae and Reoviridae.
evidence: This is demonstrated by small RNA sequencing data.

claim: The CFAV EVE insertion observed in Aag2 cells is not present in the Ae. aegypti Liverpool genome.
source: Comparing this locus with the corresponding site in the Ae. aegypti Liverpool genome, from a strain isolated in West Africa, revealed that the CFAV EVE insertion observed in Aag2 cells is not present in the mosquito genome (Figure 6B), although other CFAV-derived EVEs are found at other loci in the Ae. aegypti AaegL3 assembly (Palatini et al., 2017.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparative genome analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Other CFAV-derived EVEs are found at other loci in the Ae. aegypti AaegL3 assembly.
source: Comparing this locus with the corresponding site in the Ae. aegypti Liverpool genome, from a strain isolated in West Africa, revealed that the CFAV EVE insertion observed in Aag2 cells is not present in the mosquito genome (Figure 6B), although other CFAV-derived EVEs are found at other loci in the Ae. aegypti AaegL3 assembly (Palatini et al., 2017.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Acquisition of EVEs is a dynamic process, perhaps depending upon the geographic location and infection history of mosquito populations.
source: Thus, these observations suggest that acquisition of EVEs is a dynamic process, perhaps depending upon the geographic location and infection history of mosquito populations (Palatini et al., 2017; Olson and Bonizzoni, 2017.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed differences between Aag2 and Liverpool genomes, supported by citations.

claim: The vast majority of small RNAs mapping to EVEs are 24–30 nt in length (>95%).
source: The vast majority of small RNAs mapping to EVEs are 24–30 nt in length (>95%) and are almost exclusively antisense relative to the pseudo-ORF (>99%) (Figure 6C,i).
evidence: This is demonstrated by small RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Small RNAs mapping to EVEs are almost exclusively antisense relative to the pseudo-ORF (>99%).
source: The vast majority of small RNAs mapping to EVEs are 24–30 nt in length (>95%) and are almost exclusively antisense relative to the pseudo-ORF (>99%) (Figure 6C,i).
evidence: This is demonstrated by small RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: EVE-derived piRNAs showed a strong bias for uracil at the 1st position.
source: Furthermore, EVE-derived piRNAs showed a strong bias for uracil at the 1st position (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) and were protected from beta-elimination, suggesting that they are mature piRNAs, methylated on their 3'end (Figure 6C,i).
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: EVE-derived piRNAs were protected from beta-elimination, suggesting that they are mature piRNAs, methylated on their 3'end.
source: Furthermore, EVE-derived piRNAs showed a strong bias for uracil at the 1st position (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) and were protected from beta-elimination, suggesting that they are mature piRNAs, methylated on their 3'end (Figure 6C,i).
evidence: This is demonstrated by beta-elimination experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Knockdown of Piwi4 and Ago3, but not Ago2, resulted in a loss of EVE-derived piRNAs.
source: Importantly, knockdown of Piwi4 and Ago3, but not Ago2, resulted in a loss of EVE-derived piRNAs (Figure 6C,ii).
evidence: This is demonstrated by small RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Small RNAs derived from EVEs are bona fide piRNAs and their production requires Piwi4 and Ago3.
source: Thus, the length, methylation, and sequence bias indicate that small RNAs derived from EVEs are bona fide piRNAs and their production requires Piwi4 and Ago3.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the characterization of EVE-derived small RNAs.

claim: Piwi4-associated small RNAs mostly corresponded to CFAV EVE-derived antisense piRNAs and not to CFAV virus-derived piRNAs.
source: Strikingly, Piwi4-associated small RNAs mostly corresponded to CFAV EVE-derived antisense piRNAs and not to CFAV virus-derived piRNAs (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B) nor to TE-targeting piRNAs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoprecipitation followed by small RNA sequencing shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Piwi4 associated with significantly longer piRNAs (28–29 nt vs 26–27 nt).
source: Although most piRNAs are between 26 and 28 nt long, Piwi4 associated with significantly longer piRNAs (28–29 nt vs 26–27 nt, Xχ2, p<2.2e-16).
evidence: This is demonstrated by statistical analysis of immunoprecipitation data.

claim: During acute infection SINV-derived piRNAs bound to Piwi4 were significantly enriched for longer sequences.
source: Of note, during acute infection SINV-derived piRNAs bound to Piwi4 were also significantly enriched for longer sequences (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Piwi4 preferentially associated with longer EVE-piRNAs at the genome-wide level (28–29 nt vs 26–27 nt).
source: Similar results were obtained with the majority of piRNAs derived from EVEs identified in the Aag2 genome (Figure 6E) demonstrating that Piwi4 preferentially associated with longer EVE-piRNAs at the genome-wide level (28–29 nt vs 26–27 nt, 2, p<2.2e-16).
evidence: This is demonstrated by genome-wide analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The lack of enrichment in Piwi4 IP for the overall population of TE-targeting piRNAs suggests that Piwi4 specifically discriminates between TE-targeting and EVE-derived piRNAs.
source: The lack of enrichment in Piwi4 IP for the overall population of TE-targeting piRNAs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C) suggests that Piwi4 specifically discriminates between TE-targeting and EVE-derived piRNAs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immunoprecipitation data.

claim: TE-targeting piRNAs transcribed from piRNA clusters associated with EVEs showed no enrichment for Piwi4 binding.
source: We thus examined whether TE-targeting piRNAs transcribed from piRNA clusters associated with EVEs were preferentially bound to Piwi4 compared to TE-targeting piRNAs derived from piRNA clusters that contained only TE fragments. Like for piRNAs derived from TE-only loci, analysis of TE-targeting piRNAs transcribed from EVE containing piRNA clusters showed no enrichment for Piwi4 binding (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: piRNAs that associate with Piwi4 do not appear to be specified at the global piRNA cluster level.
source: Therefore, piRNAs that associate with Piwi4 does not appear to be specified at the global piRNA cluster level.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of TE-targeting piRNAs from different loci.

claim: Piwi4 binds preferentially to longer piRNAs and distinguishes between antiviral EVE-derived piRNAs and other piRNA cluster TE-targeting piRNAs through localized EVE-specific signals.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that Piwi4 binds preferentially to longer piRNAs and distinguishes between antiviral EVE-derived piRNAs and other piRNA cluster TE-targeting piRNAs through localized EVE-specific signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comprehensive analysis of Piwi4-associated piRNAs.

claim: CFAV EVE-derived piRNAs are efficiently loaded onto Piwi4.
source: Like antisense v-piRNAs from acute SINV infection in Aag2 cells, CFAV EVE-derived piRNAs are efficiently loaded onto Piwi4, which acts as a restriction factor against acute arboviral infections (Figure 1A and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Analysis of sense/anti-sense CFAV piRNAs showed a characteristic ping-pong processing, 10 bp offset signature.
source: Analysis of sense/anti-sense CFAV piRNAs showed a characteristic ping-pong processing, 10 bp offset signature (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that persistently infecting CFAV genome is cleaved by these anti-sense piRNAs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Persistently infecting CFAV genome is cleaved by anti-sense piRNAs.
source: Analysis of sense/anti-sense CFAV piRNAs showed a characteristic ping-pong processing, 10 bp offset signature (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that persistently infecting CFAV genome is cleaved by these anti-sense piRNAs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is inferred from the ping-pong signature observed in the piRNA data.

claim: Rluc expression was significantly reduced when the inserted EVE sequence was in the sense orientation as compared to the control antisense orientation.
source: Transfection of Rluc-EVE reporters into Aag2 cells demonstrated that Rluc expression was significantly reduced when the inserted EVE sequence was in the sense orientation as compared to the control antisense orientation (Figure 7A,ii).
evidence: This is demonstrated by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Efficiency of silencing by EVE-derived piRNAs correlated with piRNA expression levels.
source: Furthermore, efficiency of silencing correlated with piRNA expression levels (Figure 7A,i).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing silencing efficiency with piRNA abundance shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Antisense EVE-derived piRNAs can silence mRNAs containing complementary sequences.
source: Thus, antisense EVE-derived piRNAs can silence mRNAs containing complementary sequences.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reporter assay experiments.

claim: Insertion of EVE sequences in the sense orientation reduces virus replication 10 to 100 fold relative to the antisense EVE control viruses.
source: Infection of Aag2 cells with these viruses showed that insertion of EVE sequences in the sense orientation reduces virus replication 10 to 100 fold relative to the antisense EVE control viruses (Figure 7B, p<0.05 one-tail Wilcoxon rank sum test).
evidence: This is demonstrated by virus replication assays shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Piwi4 is involved in the specific inhibition of virus replication by EVE-derived piRNAs in acute infection.
source: In control cells (eGFP dsRNA), the relative viral replication advantage of the AS EVE containing virus over its S EVE counterparts increased over a 4 day time course. On the contrary, this ratio was significantly reduced at 48, 72 and 96 hr post infection (hpi) in Piwi4 knock-down Aag2 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2, Wilcoxon Signed Rank test, n = 4 independent experiments), indicating that Piwi4 is involved in the specific inhibition of virus replication by EVE-derived piRNAs in acute infection.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Piwi4 knockdown results in a significant increase in CFAV viral genome copy number.
source: To test this hypothesis, we first determined the effect of Piwi4 knockdown on CFAV persistent infection and observed a significant increase in viral genome copy number (Figure 7C, p<0.001).
evidence: This is demonstrated by qPCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Ago3 knockdown increased CFAV genome copy number.
source: Ago3 knockdown also increased CFAV genome copy number (Figure 7C, p<0.001).
evidence: This is demonstrated by qPCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Mosquito EVEs generate piRNAs capable of effectively controlling virus replication.
source: We thus conclude that mosquito EVEs generate piRNAs capable of effectively controlling virus replication.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing EVE-mediated virus inhibition.

claim: The anti-transposon surveillance pathway common to the majority of metazoan has evolved in mosquitoes as an effective adaptive antiviral defense.
source: Investigating the role of the PIWI proteins in the mosquito immune response, we found that the anti-transposon surveillance pathway common to the majority of metazoan has evolved in mosquitoes as an effective adaptive antiviral defense.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the overall findings of the study.

claim: Piwi4 appears to specifically act in the mosquito antiviral piRNA system.
source: A central player in this pathway is Piwi4, which appears to specifically act in the mosquito antiviral piRNA system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the characterization of Piwi4 function.

claim: Conversion of viral RNA genomes into vDNA is a self-nonself discriminatory process.
source: In addition, episomal DNA and genome resequencing have revealed that conversion of viral RNA genomes into vDNA is a self-nonself discriminatory process and that EVE-derived piRNAs are loaded onto Piwi4 to restrict acute and persistent infections in mosquito cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the episomal DNA sequencing data.

claim: EVE-derived piRNAs are loaded onto Piwi4 to restrict acute and persistent infections in mosquito cells.
source: In addition, episomal DNA and genome resequencing have revealed that conversion of viral RNA genomes into vDNA is a self-nonself discriminatory process and that EVE-derived piRNAs are loaded onto Piwi4 to restrict acute and persistent infections in mosquito cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.
